quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Pedestrians waiting on the sidewalk for a walk signal.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: If you parallel park facing downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep driving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is coming with lights and/or siren, move to the right side of the road and stop. Do not stop inside an intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming so you can prepare to slow down or turn.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycles?

options.text: It is okay for cars to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
Cars must move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.
Motorcycle brake lights always turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars must move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane. Before passing a motorcycle on the left, make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate with traffic merging from on-ramps on your right, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When an on-ramp is ahead, move to the left lane when safe. This gives room for vehicles to enter from the on-ramp.

questions.question: If a vehicle is driving toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left because the other driver might correct and you could still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow was pointing. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Is it illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane. Two motorcycles can share a lane, but cars cannot share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: You can ignore it in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for curves and turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for curves and turns.
questions.explanation: Warning signs for curves and turns have speed signs attached that show a recommended speed. Even if you feel comfortable driving faster in fair weather, never do so in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can turn left only after you stop.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop because the light will turn red soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and be careful. Look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is:
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Always be ready to yield to people crossing the street.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Use your turn signal, horn, and emergency lights to let other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What is the correct order of colors on a traffic light from top to bottom?
questions.explanation: Red is always at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom on a vertical traffic light. On a horizontal light, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: Can you pass on a two-lane road with a single solid yellow line on your side?
questions.explanation: You can only pass when a broken yellow line is on your side. A solid yellow line on your side means do not pass.

questions.question: What does a solid red HAWK signal mean?

options.text: You can go slowly and with caution.
You should slow down and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: HAWK signals help pedestrians cross safely. A solid red light means you must stop completely.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, look:
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your car will roll toward the curb and not into traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
There is a bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers to be careful when the pavement is wet because the road becomes slippery and vehicles are harder to control.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within eight feet of a fire hydrant. Only park where traffic is not blocked and other drivers can see your vehicle clearly from all directions.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully near bicyclists.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can easily hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is and how fast it is going. Always stay alert and careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down on slippery surfaces and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to skid, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until your vehicle is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: A fully loaded truck traveling at 55 mph could take up to ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Trucks take much longer to stop than smaller cars at the same speed. A fully loaded truck traveling at 55 mph may need almost 400 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: You and another driver arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. The driver is on your left. Who goes first?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic clearly. This helps you know what is around you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles are often hidden in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before turning or changing lanes on residential streets. Signal five seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.
